To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multivariable model including the levels of seven biomarkers measured in the preoperative blood of prostate cancer patients improves the prediction of biochemical recurrence following surgery, and that this model has excellent calibration and discriminative power.

the preoperative blood levels for a panel of seven biomarkers, including TGF-β, IL-6 and sIL-6, VEGF and VCAM-1 and uPA, improve the accuracy of standard clinical predictors to predict biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy for clinically localized prostate cancers.
we have developed a nomogram that predicts the risk of biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy based on preoperative plasma levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to the development of biomarker panels for predicting the outcome of patients treated for prostate cancer.
a new method for predicting disease relapse after radical prostatectomy through a panel of preoperative blood-based biomarkers.
the development of a novel, highly sensitive, and specific diagnostic method for prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study shows that a panel of preoperative plasma-based biomarkers improves the prediction of biochemical relapse after radical prostatectomy, and that this improvement is clinically relevant, and may be of value for counseling patients and for the design of future trials.
a panel of pre-operative blood based biomarkers can be used in conjunction with the established predictors to improve the accuracy of prediction of disease relapse after radical prostatectomy.
the use of a panel of preoperative biomarkers may improve the accuracy of the standard predictive model for biochemical recurrence following radical surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a panel of preoperative plasma biomarkers improves the ability of a standard nomogram to predict disease recurrence following radical prostatection.
a panel of biomarkers may help identify patients at risk of recurrence after radical prostatectomy, and these biomarkers are independent of the established clinical variables.

the addition of a panel of biomarkers to a standard multivariable model increases the predictive accuracy of this model for biochemical recurrence following radical treatment for clinically localized prostate carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a panel of biomarkers, including TGF-β, sIL-1, VCAM- 1, uPA, and VEGF, can help predict biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer.
the preoperative blood levels for these biomarkers may allow more accurate prediction of biochemical recurrence following surgery.
a panel of preoperative blood-based biomarkers improves the predictive accuracy of standard clinical predictors of prostate cancer recurrence following radical prostatectionomy.
